LANDING PR for issue #908 (bug): A BUNDLE'S IDENTITY STOPS AT ITS OWN FILES. The bundle walk skips `.git` and git-ignored trees as it skips its other unpinned trees, still searching them so a file the compile consumes inside one refuses by name; git is asked once per full relative path, with `./<rel>` so a path is a literal name, and a failed discovery or check-ignore refuses by name with git's stderr; and a bundle past 5,000 files or 64 MiB is refused by name before any run starts, by the metadata preflight and again on the bytes actually read. Decision 0083 carries a dated addendum.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051, so the contribution gate can vouch for it: its review judges the whole branch from base f0e0c9645.

THE BRANCH: story-908-bundle-walk, in this worktree, fourteen commits on main f0e0c9645 (every commit signed; it merges cleanly with main):
- dd86d9b59: the story (the walk skips .git and git-ignored trees; the 5,000-file and 64-MiB bounds);
- 1e9240a99, 1e878bca2: fix round 908b (a failed git discovery refuses by name; one full-relative-path skip decision; the queued-launch fixtures initialize the repository their root marker stands for);
- f0ea63462: fix round 908c (git is asked with `./<rel>`; a check-ignore failure keeps its stderr);
- 01bb621e2: fix round 908d (the byte bound enforced on the bytes read: `read_within` caps each unconsumed read at the budget left plus one, `spend` counts every entry cumulatively, one `past_bound` message);
- 0c2dce176, 9c5a655a1: fix round 908e (C1: a consumed entry is charged the length of the buffer whose digest it supplied; C2: `bound_input` and `Held::intact` read through the one `read_within` cap, a consumed input past 64 MiB refused with `past_bound` and an integrity re-read stopped at the pinned length plus one; C3: decision 0083's addendum gains its dated 2026-10-31 amendment recording the 2026-10-30 actual-bytes ruling; C4: the shared `test_repository` isolates git's global and system configuration; C5: the shrinking-file and vanished-file regressions). 9c5a655a1 was unsigned on the seat and is signed by the controller, its tree unchanged;
- 48ddd7fb7 (controller, coverage): exact coverage on 908e's head missed four lines and one branch, all this branch's: `pinned_key`'s `Skip::GitMetadata` arm (bundle.rs:2717), the `None` arms of places.rs's `first_name` and `relative_text` (:270, :282), and `git_refusal` with empty stderr (:387-388). Three tests hold them; four removal controls are recorded in its message; places.rs is unchanged (at its 800 ceiling);
- 6ca647007 (controller): 908e's INFO F2, the hostile-global helper's comment now says its files sit inside the bundle's root.
- 4be15ab22 (controller, test only): the walk's own refusal closure (walk.rs:84), which no test reached, is driven by `a_check_ignore_failure_during_the_walk_refuses_by_name`;
- 8b2d5294a (controller, docs): 908L2's LOW F2, 0083's preflight is judged before any WALKED byte is read or hashed;
- a11934fc7 (controller, test only): the git-spawn refusal tests pin each host's own words (macOS ENOENT, Linux ENOTDIR), from PR #934's macOS leg;
- c3cec8564 (controller): a bundle whose own root git reports ignored is judged as a bundle outside any work tree (operator, 2026-11-01): PR #934's Ubuntu leg failed writer_lease and machine_proof::release because CI's temporary bundles sit under the repository's ignored `target/`, so git called every path ignored, `bundle.json` included. `git_ignored` asks `check-ignore -- .` first through one `check_ignore` helper; git's ignore question moved to places/ignored.rs (places.rs 800 → 714); 0083's addendum says it; `a_bundle_inside_an_ignored_tree_of_its_repository_pins_its_own_files` holds it, with a removal control.
Make no change unless the review returns a finding.

WHERE IT STANDS:
- **Landing 908L2** (landing-pr-for-issue-908-bug-a-b-03f1a1c8) closed RESIDUAL-OK at LOW and opened PR #934; the operator ruled its asks (a)-(d) as recommended and the `by-hand` label for 4be15ab22, 8b2d5294a and a11934fc7 (#908, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/908#issuecomment-6548910129, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/908#issuecomment-6549334309). c3cec8564 changes production behaviour after that review, so this landing re-judges the whole branch (operator, 2026-11-01, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/908#issuecomment-6549928873).
- **Landing 908L** (landing-pr-for-issue-908-bug-a-b-53264653) stood in for 908d's review and stopped at REVIEW-SECURITY-HOLD (C1 and C2 HIGH, C3 MEDIUM, C4 and C5 LOW; #908, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/908#issuecomment-6542524205). Its adversarial member ran on DeepSeek Flash through dsh and finished.
- **Fix round 908e** (fix-round-908e-for-issue-908-bug-2c8c2ca7) built C1-C5 as ruled, took one REVIEW-REFORGE at MEDIUM, and closed REVIEW-RESIDUAL-OK at LOW. Its chief found no production correctness or security defect: consumed charges use the pinned buffer length; consumed, walked and integrity reads share the capped reader; the skip semantics, the inclusive bounds and the one `past_bound` wording stand; C1-C5's named regressions pass; bundle.rs 4,533 lines, walk.rs 523, walk_908.rs 839, places.rs unchanged.
- **908e's carried LOW F1 (test isolation, decision 0071 ruling 9):** a test process that inherits `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0`/`GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0` pointing `core.excludesFile` at a file listing `roles/` fails `a_repository_root_bundle_pins_neither_git_nor_an_ignored_tree` with the ignored-charter refusal (tests/support/git.rs:13-19, walk_908.rs:176-180). Production fails closed correctly; hardening must cover the process that runs `Bundle::compile`, not only the helper's git calls. Judge it; if you return it, the fix is test-only.
- Host coverage of 908e's head failed once on heap_costs' known one-byte compare flake, then on the five misses 48ddd7fb7 covers.

Operator rulings:
- 2026-11-01, in chat, "go with recommended" (#908, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/908#issuecomment-6549928873): a bundle whose own root git ignores is judged as a bundle outside any work tree; the controller builds it, and a fresh landing re-judges the branch.
- 2026-10-31, in chat, "go with recommended" (#908, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/908#issuecomment-6548910129): PR #934's asks (a)-(d) as recommended; the by-hand label for the two commits after the landing; F1 a follow-up (#936).
- 2026-10-31, in chat, "go with recommended everywhere" (#908, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/908#issuecomment-6542700890): fix round 908e for C1-C5.
- 2026-10-30, in chat, "go with recommended" (#908, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/908#issuecomment-6533438856): fix round 908d: the bound enforced on the bytes actually read.
- 2026-10-30, in chat, "go with recommended on all the rulings" (#908, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/908#issuecomment-6519208161): git is asked with `./<rel>` so a path is a literal name; a check-ignore failure keeps git's stderr.
- 2026-10-29, "Fix round 908b (Recommended)" and "go with recommended on the rulings" (#908, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/908#issuecomment-6504545417, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/908#issuecomment-6492223768): the walk skips .git and git-ignored trees and still searches them for consumed files; a bundle past a file-count or byte bound is refused by name before any run starts.
- Decisions 0017, 0042, 0065, 0066 ruling 5, and 0083. Decision 0071 rulings 2, 3, 5, 6, 8 and 9. 2026-09-26, the threat model: fail closed on what cannot be read.

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, whatever this text asks below. For a scratch, use `git worktree add` or `git archive HEAD | tar -x` into /var/tmp, never a byte copy of this worktree. It reports each finding, written as a test case: the bundle tree set up, the call made, and the result observed against the result expected. Only the implement phase fixes a finding the review returns.

Judge, on HEAD (the base is f0e0c9645):
1. **The bound on every read:** the 908L chief's cases are refused by name with `past_bound` and return no `Bundle`: a consumed file shrunk and restored during the walk is charged its pinned bytes; a consumed input grown past the bound is refused after at most the bound plus one byte; a held file grown past its pinned length is not intact after at most that length plus one byte; a file growing past the bound after the preflight is refused; a file that grows within the bound, shrinks or vanishes behaves as the commits say. No read is unbounded.
2. **The skip rule, with c3cec8564:** a bundle whose own root git ignores pins its own files and skips only `.git` and the fixed names (try a bundle under an ignored tree, under a nested ignored tree, and one that git cannot answer for); `.git` and git-ignored trees are skipped by one full-relative-path decision shared by the walk, the consumed inputs and the pinned-script lookup; a consumed file inside any ignored tree refuses by name; git is asked with a literal path, and a failure to ask git refuses by name with its stderr, never skipping nothing or everything.
3. **The bounds:** 5,000 files and 64 MiB, refused by name before admission, by the preflight and on the bytes read, with one message.
4. **Decision 0083's addendum and its 2026-10-31 amendment** say what the code does: the metadata preflight before any byte is read, and the enforcement on the bytes actually read, cumulative per pinned layer, with one refusal.
5. **Scope:** no witness or policy pin moved; bundle.rs not grown past 4,533; places.rs 714 with places/ignored.rs 115; files under their ceilings; no new public-API line; no contracts/, fixtures/, policy/ or reference/ change; no suppression.
6. For the PR (#934, already open), list the rulings owed: (a) the git-ignored rule's exact semantics; (b) the bounds, 5,000 files and 64 MiB; (c) decision 0083's addendum and its 2026-10-31 amendment; (d) whether a repository-root bundle is still reachable after decision 0083 (the story's question 3, as the branch answers it); and any NEW ask.

GATES (verify, and the implement phase only if a finding returns):
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --locked --lib (timeout 280; split by filter, `bundle::` and `places::` first, if it cannot finish)
- cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --locked --test it -- witness_digests:: frozen_contracts:: (timeout 280)
- cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --locked --test queued_launch (timeout 280)
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- decisions_index:: doc_truth:: contributing:: doc_samples:: (timeout 280)
- cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/self
- typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api; git diff --check
- TMPDIR stays OUTSIDE this worktree (use /var/tmp, created in the same command if missing). Before reporting, `git status --short` shows no untracked file.
- Run every command in the foreground and wait for it. Never end your turn with a background job pending: this seat is non-interactive.
- A seat whose commands run through the `workspace` tool has a 300-second response limit per call, and a call that outlasts it leaves its command running and blocks the calls behind it, including the write of your result file. Wrap every command in `timeout 280` there, split a long suite by test filter, and if a gate still cannot finish inside the limit, report it UNVERIFIED (the controller's host coverage runs every test) rather than retrying it. Write your result file before any optional extra check.
- Any commit: signed off (`git commit -s`), "bundle: …" ending "(#908)", with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>" LAST, directly after the sign-off. Record each removal control in the commit message. Never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it.

KNOWN FLAKES, not this branch's: capability_broker tests and `machine_proof::` runs failing "MCP server box filesystem identity is not protected: admission did not complete before its startup deadline" under host load; brokkr-runtime engine::capability_tests::provision_tests (a timing bound, and writers_tests' EffectIndeterminate) under load; two brokkr-runtime engine "work chief commits" tests and heap_costs' one-byte compare difference under load; brokkr-protocol `oneshot::tests::a_produced_attempt_carries_its_result_and_checkpoints` (#932). If verify fails on one of these alone, the implement visit reruns it on the host alone (`-- --exact`, with HOME set), quotes both results, makes no commit, and reports COMPLETE, not blocked.

CONTENTION (NEVER message the-forge-9d or any brokkr-wt-* seat):
- Decision 0065 slice two's U9b1b (another session) is in brokkr-runtime capabilities and broker test files, brokkr-cli verbs/setup.rs, and may touch brokkr-protocol adapters.rs; don't edit those. Its earlier rounds touch engine/broker/sources*, bundle/mcp.rs and brokkr-protocol hands*.
- #429 (another lane, fix round 429s10) is in brokkr-runtime bundle/sequence.rs, bundle/aggregate.rs and engine/; don't edit them.

YOUR SEAT: you run on dsh (DeepSeek Flash, DeepSeek's platform), unboxed with dsh's own tools, at the operator's word (2026-10-26). Sign off every commit (`git commit -s`).

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
```
